title: Monoidal and adjunction normalization of derived ringed-topos comparisons
statement:
Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be morphisms of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], presented by sites small in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaves of commutative rings $A_X,A_Y,A_Z$. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the K-flat derived tensor and pullbacks of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and the K-injective direct images and normalized comparisons $\kappa_{g,f}:R(gf)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*Rf_*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Write $P_h=Lh^*$, $R_h=Rh_*$, and give $P_h\dashv R_h$ the canonical derived adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Write $t_h:P_h(U\otimes^L V)\xrightarrow{\sim}P_hU\otimes^LP_hV$ for the canonical tensor comparison, and $e_h:P_hA_{\mathrm{target}}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\mathrm{source}}$ for its unit comparison.

These comparisons make $P_h$ a symmetric strong monoidal functor: $t_h,e_h$ commute with the derived tensor associators, both unitors, and the symmetry. The associator is induced by $(x\otimes y)\otimes z\mapsto x\otimes(y\otimes z)$ and the symmetry by $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ in degrees $p,q$.

There is a canonical comparison $c_{f,g}:P_{gf}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_fP_g$, computed by ordinary module pullback composition on K-flat complexes with flat terms. It is monoidal: for $U,V\in D(A_Z)$,
$$t_{f;P_gU,P_gV}\circ P_f(t_{g;U,V})\circ c_{f,g,U\otimes^LV}=(c_{f,g,U}\otimes^Lc_{f,g,V})\circ t_{gf;U,V},$$
and $e_f\circ P_f(e_g)\circ c_{f,g,A_Z}=e_{gf}$. The comparison $\kappa_{g,f}$ is adjunction-compatible: under $c_{f,g}$ and $\kappa_{g,f}$ the canonical adjunction for $gf$ is the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. In particular its counit is
$$\varepsilon_{gf,E}=\varepsilon_{f,E}\circ P_f(\varepsilon_{g,R_fE})$$
under those comparisons. The canonical comparisons $P_{\mathrm{id}}\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $R_{\mathrm{id}}\cong\mathrm{id}$ identify the tensor comparisons and the adjunction with those of the identity functor and identity adjunction. Finally, if two ringed-topos morphisms with the same source and target are related by a 2-isomorphism of their underlying geometric morphisms whose structural ring maps commute with that 2-isomorphism, then this specified isomorphism induces a monoidal isomorphism of their derived pullbacks and the corresponding adjunction-compatible isomorphism of their derived direct images. All these assertions hold without flatness of the structural ring maps or boundedness of the complexes.
